convoLines.text: "Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"I regret the ordinary days I rushed through. All those Vancouver, Canada mornings I spent annoyed at small things. I'd pay anything for one annoyed morning now."
"Still on your regrets."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took Zoltan — The Blood Tithe, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I write everything down. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it. Seen worse."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
"Me? I laughed yesterday and it scared me — the sound of it. Like my body remembered something my head hadn't approved. Laughter's a mutiny. A good one."
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen."
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"The Blood Tithe. They just... took Zoltan. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
They light up a little when they see you.
"My part? I carry water to the sick row. Someone has to."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them American Persimmon — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Mm. Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We went over this," Wei says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"That again?" Wei sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Actually, forget it."
"Mayapple — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Ray doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "I know you and Hunter were close. I'm sorry."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can we talk?" Wei sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
At the cache spot the ground is torn up. Something was here, recently, and it wasn't careful. Wei's hand finds your sleeve. You leave together, faster than you came.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Hunter owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"I keep turning over the last thing Hunter said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
